_meta.section: Living as Christians Part 7 — Discussion: "Follow the Course of Hospitality"
_meta.anchor_question: How do we benefit when we extend hospitality to those outside our circle of close friends? (data-pid 39)

underlines.phrase: Jehovah is the best example of hospitality

notes.content: You know how you feel after you do something nice for somebody who'd never do it back? Like you held the door for somebody at the gas station and they didn't even nod — but somehow you walk to your car feeling lighter? That's the benefit. Notice Acts 14:17 — Jehovah gives rain and fruitful seasons to people who don't even know him yet. He's the original example. He extends hospitality to people who aren't going to thank him for it. When we copy that, we're not just helping the other person. We're stretching our own heart bigger. Hospitality outside our circle isn't really for them. It's for us — to keep us from shrinking down to only loving the people who love us back.
